column2: To Rudra, destroyer of Tripura, and Bhani — the two shanks; "Shiva, to Rudra, to Ishvara, to Vijaya" — the knees;
To Isha — the hip of the Goddess; "to Shankara" — Shankara; the two sides "to Kotavi," the trident-bearer "to Shulapani";
Homage to Mangala — one should worship the belly; "homage to the Self of all" — Rudra; "to Ishani" — the two breasts;
Shiva "to the Self of gods," likewise "to Hladini" — one should worship the throat; "to Mahadeva" Shiva; "to Ananta" the two hands;
to the three-eyed — Hara; the arm "to the beloved of Kalanala"; "to Saubhagya, to Mahesha" one should worship the ornaments;
to Ashoka-madhuvasini, to Ishvara the two lips; the face "to Chaturmukhapriya, to Hara, homage to Sthanu";
homage to Ardhanarisha-Hara, to Amitangi the nose; "homage to Ugra, lord of the world," and again the brows "to Lalita";
to Sarva, destroyer of the cities, to Vasanti the palate; "homage to Shrikanthanatha, to Shitikantha" the hair;
to Bhimograya, to Supupini the head; "homage to the Self of all." Mallika, ashoka, lotus, kunda, tagara, malati,
kadamba, oleander, vana, amlana, saffron, sinduvara — in all months in order are remembered.
Having worshipped Uma and Maheshvara, one should place before them the eight good-fortune items: ghee, nishpava, safflower, milk, jivaka,
tree-king, sugarcane, salt, and kustumburu the eighth. In Chaitra having drunk water with horn, one should sleep before the God and Goddess.
In the morning having bathed and worshipped one should worship a Brahmin couple. One should give those eight to a Brahmin: "May Lalita be pleased with me."
Horn water, cow-dung, mandara, bilva leaf, kusha water, curds, milk in Kartika, spotted ghee,
cow-urine and ghee, black sesame, the five cow-products — food in order. Lalita, Vijaya, Bhadra, Bhavani, Kumuda, Shiva,
Vasudevi and Gauri, Mangala, Kamala, Sati — at the time of gifts from Chaitra and so on one should say "May she be pleased."
At the end of the vow one should give a fruit, a pure ghee, and a bed; a golden Uma-Maheshvara and a bull with a cow;
having worshipped the teacher and couples with garments and the rest, one shares enjoyment and liberation. Good fortune, health, beauty, life — the good-fortune-bed vows
one should perform in Bhadrapada or Vaishakha or Margashirsha. On the third of the bright half one should worship "homage to Lalita";
each fortnight then worshipping, at the end of the vow also couples; having worshipped twenty-four with garments and the rest one shares enjoyment and liberation.
This is stated as the second way; I tell the Saubhagya vow: from the third of Phalguna he who avoids salt,
at the end should give a bed with household articles; having worshipped a Brahmin couple: "May Bhavani be pleased."
For good fortune the third is told, giving Gauri's world and the rest; one who keeps the third-vow in Magha, Bhadra and Vaishakha;
the Damanaka-third doer in Chaitra should worship with damanaka; the Atma-third of Margashirsha one should worship by eating as desired and so on.
Gauri, Kali, Uma, Bhadra, Durga, Kanti, Sarasvati, Vaishnavi, Lakshmi, Prakriti, Shiva, Narayani in order;
beginning from the Margashirsha third, one obtains good fortune and heaven.
Since Krishna was born on it, the eighth is Jayanti; one is freed from sin done in seven births by fasting.
On the eighth in the dark half of Bhadrapada joined with Rohini, having fasted one should worship Krishna, giver of enjoyment and liberation:

I invoke Krishna, Balabhadra, Devaki, Vasudeva, Yashoda and Gopa; I worship; homage to you.
agnipuran:183:5	Homage, homage to Yoga, lord of yoga, Yogesha; homage, homage to Govinda, the source of yoga and the rest.
One should give a bath to Krishna and have arghya given with this: "Homage to Yajna, lord of sacrifice, master of sacrifices;
homage, homage to Govinda, the source of sacrifice and the rest. Accept, god, these fragrant flowers dear to you;
be giver of all desires to me, god praised by gods. You who are perfumed by incense, accept this incense by the perfumed;
make me fragrant with incense-scent, Hari; shining lamp, great lamp, giver of light, always,
accept what is given by me and make me move upward. Homage, homage to the universe, lord of the universe, Vishvesha;
to Govinda, the source of the universe and the rest, it is offered. Homage, homage to Dharma, lord of dharma, Dharmesha;
to Govinda the source of dharma, make rest. Homage, homage to Sarva, lord of all, Sarvesha;
to Govinda, the source of all and the rest, purification. Born of the milk-ocean, born of Atri's eye,
accept, Shashanka, this arghya, with Rohini, for me." One should install the god on a platform and worship the moon with Rohini:
Devaki, Vasudeva, Yashoda, Nanda and Bala. At midnight one should pour streams with jaggery and ghee;
the vower should give garments, gold and the like, and feed Brahmins. The doer of the Janmashtami vow has sons and shares Vishnu's world.
One who does it year after year seeking sons knows no fear: "Give sons, give wealth, life, health, offspring,
dharma, desire, good fortune, heaven and liberation give me."
I shall tell the Krishnashtami vow: one should do it in the month of Margashirsha. Having made it a night-meal, pure, one should drink cow-urine at night,
sleeping on the ground at night, the vower should worship Shankara. In Pausha Shambhu, having tasted ghee; in Magha Maheshvara with milk;
Mahadeva in Phalguna, fasting, eating sesame; in Chaitra Sthanu, eating barley; in Vaishakha then worship Shiva;
eating kusha-water, Pashupati; in Jyeshtha eating horn-water; in Ashadha eating cow-dung, Ugra; in Shravana Sarva, eating arka;
Tryambaka in Bhadrapada, eating bilva leaf at night; in Ashvina Isha, eating rice; in Kartika Rudra;
eating curds, doing oblation; at the end of the year one should worship in the mandala; one should give a cow, cloth and gold to the teacher and to Brahmins likewise;
having fed Brahmins by request one obtains enjoyment and liberation. A night-eater on the eighths should give a cow at year's end;
he goes to Indra's station — the heaven-going vow is so called. When the eighth falls on Wednesday in both fortnights,
then one should do the vow, or one with jaggery. Those who keep the rule on it do not lose their prosperity.
Excluding two fingers of eight handfuls of rice, having made food in a mango-leaf cup with kusha, with Kula and Ambika,
having worshipped the sattvic limb one should eat while hearing the tale. According to ability one should give a fee: a cucumber with rice.
There was a steadfast Brahmin; his wife was Rambha, his son Kaushika; his daughter Vijaya; the steadfast one's bull gave wealth.
Kaushika, taking that bull to graze with cowherds, at the time of bathing in the Ganga the bull was carried off by thieves.
Having bathed, not seeing the bull, he came to search for the bull; with his sister Vijaya he saw in a lake
a group of divine women; he said, "Give food." The group of women said: "Eat, you are a vower, since you are a guest."
Having done the vow he ate and found the forest-keeper; the steadfast one went with the bull and with Vijaya then.
Vijaya was given by the steadfast one to Yama; the father was removed; by the feeling of the vow Kaushika became king in Ayodhya.
Having seen the parents in hell, Vijaya went to Yama in distress; to the hunting Kaushika she said: "How are they freed from hell?"
Yama said: "By two vows"; having obtained that, Kaushika gave the fruit of two Wednesday-eighths; then the parents went to heaven.
Vijaya, delighted, kept the vow for enjoyment and the rest. Those who drink eight ashoka buds in Punarvasu
on the bright eighth in Chaitra do not meet sorrow: "You, remover of sorrow, desired, born in the spring month,
I drink, afflicted by sorrow; make me always sorrowless." One who does mother-worship on the eighth from Chaitra conquers enemies.
The ninth called Pishtaka, eating flour, from worship of the gods. When on the bright eighth in Ashvina the sun is in Virgo, at the root-star,
the Mahati ninth is remembered as always destroying sin. Durga, standing in nine houses or in one house,
is worshipped with eighteen arms, the rest with sixteen hands; the rest would be sixteen-handed with collyrium and drum.
Rudrachanda, Prachanda, Chandogra, Chandanayika, Chanda, Chandavati are to be worshipped, Chandarupa, Atichandika;
in order in the middle Ugrachanda, Durga the slayer of the buffalo. "Om Durge Durge, protect, svaha" is the ten-syllable mantra;
beginning with the long-vowel mantra, nine-eyed, ending in "namah"; with six words "namah, svadha, vashat" the heart and the rest;
having placed the limbs from thumb to little finger one should repeat to Shiva. One who repeats this secret is not obstructed by anyone.
Bearing in the left hands a skull, shield, bell, mirror, forefinger, bow, banner, drum, noose,
spear, club, trident, thunderbolt, sword and lance, conch, discus, arrow — one should worship the weapons.
Having repeated "Kali, Kali" over an animal one should slay it with a sword: "Kali, Kali, lady of thunderbolt, homage to the iron-staffed."
The blood and flesh from it to Putana in the southwest; in the northwest to Papa-Rakshasi, Charaki; homage in the northeast;
to Vidarika in the southeast, Mahakaushika to Agni; in front of it the king should bathe; one should take away an enemy of flour.
One should give to Skanda and Vishakha; at night one should worship Brahmani and the others: Jayanti, Mangala, Kali, Bhadrakali, Kapalini,
Durga, Shiva, Kshama, Dhatri, Svaha, Svadha — homage to you. Having bathed the Goddess with five nectars one should worship with offerings and the rest;
banners and the rest, chariot processions and the rest, offerings, boons and so on.
There a hundred sacrifices' merit at the breaking of the fast on the thirteenth. A tenth mixed with an eleventh is not to be fasted; it gives hell.
Fasting on the eleventh and eating on the next day, I shall eat, Pundarikaksha; be my refuge, Achyuta.
When on the bright eleventh the star is Pushya, that is to be fasted; it gives imperishable fruit and is called sin-destroying.
An eleventh or twelfth joined with Shravana is called Vijaya, giving victory to devotees.
This same in the month of Phalguna joined with Pushya is called Vijaya by the good, crores upon crores better.
On the eleventh worship of Vishnu is to be done, benefiting all; he becomes rich and has sons, and is honored in Vishnu's world.
He who gives on the bright twelfth is the giver of all flavors. One should worship a calf in Bhadrapada — the Govatsa-dvadashi vower.
When Magha has passed, the twelfth joined with Shravana in the dark half is called Tila-dvadashi.
Bathing with sesame, oblation with sesame, offering of sesame sweets, a lamp with sesame oil, and sesame water should be given;
sesame should be given to Brahmins; the fruit from oblation and fasting. "Om, homage to the Lord Vasudeva" — one should worship.
